title: Lower bound for the min-cut survival product
statement:
Let $C$ be a minimum cut of a multigraph $G$, and write $n$ for its number of vertices; suppose $n \ge 4$. Then
\[
  \frac{2}{n(n-1)} \;\le\; \prod_{i=0}^{n-3} \frac{n-i-2}{n-i}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a cut of the multigraph $G$
replaced:
Let $C$ be a minimum cut of a multigraph $G$ with $n = \abs{V(G)} \ge 4$. Then the
telescoping product of per-step survival factors, which represents the probability that
none of the $n-2$ contractions picks a cut edge, is bounded below by
\[
  \frac{2}{n(n-1)} \;\le\; \prod_{i=0}^{n-3} \frac{n - i - 2}{n - i} .
\]
